hints.title: Daily Grouping by Make
hints.text: Aggregate distinct leads and partners for each unique combination of date and make name.

hints.title: Grouping Keys
hints.text: group the records by date_id and make_name.

hints.title: Distinct Value Counting
hints.text: use count(distinct lead_id) and count(distinct partner_id) to count unique entities per group.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT date_id, make_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT lead_id) AS unique_leads,
       COUNT(DISTINCT partner_id) AS unique_partners
FROM DailySales
GROUP BY date_id, make_name;
```

variables: G: distinct date and make groups
complexity.notes: Hashes composite date and make keys to aggregate distinct leads and partners.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard COUNT without DISTINCT overcounts repeated sales leads and partner transactions on the same day.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Group by with distinct aggregation hashes keys and values in O(N) time and compact memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize simple multi-column group by and multiple COUNT(DISTINCT col) aggregations.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def daily_leads_and_partners(daily_sales: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    res = daily_sales.groupby(['date_id', 'make_name']).agg(
        unique_leads=('lead_id', 'nunique'),
        unique_partners=('partner_id', 'nunique')
    ).reset_index()
    return res
